newsitem.title: USA: Scattered buying pushes US mortgage-backeds higher.
newsitem.headline: Scattered buying pushes US mortgage-backeds higher.

text.p: A smattering of buying late in the afternoon pulled U.S. mortgage-backed securities out of their Tuesday morning doldrums, market sources said.
Steady selling in pass-throughs held prices in negative territory most of the day, but a spurt of afternoon buying reversed the losses and pushed prices higher, they said.
"It's been an active day," said one trader at a New York Investment firm.
"We saw some heavy selling in Ginnie Mae 8.0s and 7.0s in the morning and then there was a smatter of buying," he said.
By late afternoon pass-throughs were unchanged to three ticks higher, and yield spreads to Treasuries were mostly unchanged.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 3/32 at 100-19/32, yielding 98 basis points above the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 3/32 higher as well, at 100-14/32 and 100-19/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 4/32 at 100-16/32 to yield 6.43 percent.
Federal Reserve policy makers were meeting Tuesday and Wednesday to determine the appropriate level of short-term interest rates, but most Wall Street analysts expect the outcome to be status quo.
Looking forward, one trader said he is expecting market activity to slow down until the January payroll number is released on Friday.
"We're going to put everything off until the employment number," he said.
